articles.summary: Reusable pod and affordable training round demonstrated for the U.S. ArmyTUCSON, Ariz., Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, demonstrated its DeepStrikeTM JR3 solution for the U.S. Army's Joint Reduced Range Rocket program during a third successful flight test. DeepStrike JR3 is designed to replace the U.S. Army's Reduced Range Practice Rocket. The latest test reinforces the system's reliability, affordability and readiness to meet the U.S. Army's growing training requirements.During the recent test at Yuma Proving Ground, Ariz., Raytheon rapidly fired multiple JR3 rounds and demonstrated several key performance attributes, including launch pod container reusability and maintainability, range, trajectory, accuracy and visibility of the marking solution to increase training effectiveness.
articles.title: RTX's Raytheon advances Joint Reduced Range Rocket with third successful flight test

articles.summary: New technology to help operators detect and respond to threats fasterARLINGTON, Va., Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has been awarded a phase one contract from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) to develop an all-optical processing system for the Photonic Integrated Circuit Architectures for Scalable System Objectives, or PICASSO, program.Under the contract, Raytheon's Advanced Technology team will design and demonstrate new photonic circuit technology that uses light rather than electricity to process signals. This means operators can detect threats sooner, respond more quickly and maintain better situational awareness in contested environments.
articles.title: RTX's Raytheon to develop new optical signal processing capability
